findings.summary: The pinned corpus exposed Doe rejecting WGSL vector-scalar compound assignment. Semantic analysis and IR validation now apply the underlying binary-operation rules, and the unchanged Doe workload completes without native compiler diagnostics.

Doe passes every clean-process run of the unchanged upstream assertion and generated-shader corpus on the bound physical AMD Vulkan adapter without crashes, timeouts, or native shader compilation failures.

The pinned Node/Dawn provider aborts during adapter probing and every clean test process around its WGSL-language-feature binding, so it supplies no complete comparator identity or successful workload row on this host.
Doe's application result is retained as compatibility evidence, but the comparator crash prevents structural equivalence, reliability comparison, performance comparison, or a replacement claim.

limitations: The pinned incumbent provider crashes before it can produce complete adapter identity or a successful workload process.
The workload validates generated shader compilation and process stability but does not dispatch the generated functions or verify semantic output values.
The application harness is diagnostic and is not a promoted release dependency.
No performance claim is allowed because the incumbent did not complete equivalent work.

performance.reason: The pinned comparator crashed and the workload is compilation-only, so process durations are not a fair operation-speed comparison.
